title: Requests, People, and Body Words at R4

lessons.title: Water and tea requests return at R4
lessons.headword: ਪਾਣੀ, ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕਰਕੇ · ਚਾਹ, ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕਰਕੇ
lessons.romanization: pāṇī, kirpā karke · cāh, kirpā karke
lessons.gloss: retrieve water and tea requests with their old source and tone cues at R4

segments.text: Ask for water, then tea, using the same known polite close each time.
Read ਪਾਣੀ, ਚਾਹ once. This is recognition and spoken retrieval, not a writing checkpoint.

segments.prompt: Say Water, please and Tea, please in Punjabi. Keep cāh high and level rather than pronouncing a final h consonant.
acceptedResponses: pāṇī, kirpā karke; cāh, kirpā karke
paani kirpa karke; chaah kirpa karke

feedback.correct: Both polite requests and tea's high level tone returned.
feedback.incorrect: Repair one request, then say the pair again.

segments.prompt: Which drink is inherited from the old root meaning drink, and which came overland from Chinese through Persian?
acceptedResponses: pāṇī is inherited from the drink root; cāh came overland from chinese through persian
water - drink root; tea - chinese through persian

feedback.correct: The inherited word and the loan route stayed separate.
feedback.incorrect: Keep inherited drink with pāṇī; overland Chinese loan with cāh.

segments.text: Make the two polite requests once more from meaning.

lessons.title: Milk and bread return at R4
lessons.gloss: retrieve milk and bread with honest source limits at R4

segments.text: Hear dudh, roṭī and say “milk, bread” aloud.
Read ਦੁੱਧ, ਰੋਟੀ once. No copying is requested, and no independent writing evidence is awarded.

segments.prompt: Say the meanings aloud in order: dudh / roṭī.

feedback.incorrect: Repair only the missed noun, then say the pair again.

segments.prompt: Which word descends from dugdha, that which has been milked, and which is inherited from roṭikā while its deeper root remains unsettled?
acceptedResponses: dudh descends from dugdha; roṭī descends from roṭikā and has an unsettled deeper root
milk - dugdha; bread - rotika, deeper root unknown

feedback.correct: The known milk history and the honest bread limit returned.
feedback.incorrect: Keep dugdha with milk; roṭikā plus an unsettled deeper root with bread.

segments.text: Ask for either one using the already-known kirpā karke.

lessons.title: Friend and family return at R4
lessons.gloss: retrieve friend and family with their distinct source stories at R4

segments.text: Read ਦੋਸਤ, ਪਰਿਵਾਰ once. The models support reading only; do not count them as independent writing.

segments.prompt: Say the meanings aloud in order: dost / parivār.

feedback.incorrect: Repair one meaning, then say the pair again.

segments.prompt: Match the old images: the chosen one from Persian; pari around plus the root cover or surround.
acceptedResponses: dost — the chosen one from persian; parivār — what surrounds you
friend - chosen; family - what surrounds you

feedback.correct: The Persian chosen friend and Sanskrit surrounding family stayed distinct.
feedback.incorrect: Keep chosen with dost and surrounds with parivār.

lessons.title: Brother, sister, and eye return at R4
lessons.gloss: retrieve brother, sister, and eye with tone and doubling contrasts at R4

segments.text: Say bharā, bhaiṇ, and akkh from memory: brother, sister, eye. Keep the first two low; hold the doubled consonant in the third.
Read ਭਰਾ, ਭੈਣ, ਅੱਖ once. This lesson deliberately stops at reading and speech; it does not award independent Gurmukhi writing evidence.

segments.prompt: Say brother / sister / eye in Punjabi. Which two begin with the already-taught low-tone outcome, and which keeps a real doubled consonant?
acceptedResponses: bharā / bhaiṇ / akkh; brother and sister have the low-tone outcome; akkh keeps the doubled consonant
bhara / bhain / akkh; first two low; akkh doubled

feedback.correct: The three meanings and the old tone-versus-doubling contrast returned.
feedback.incorrect: Repair one word, then keep low tone with the kin words and doubling with akkh.

segments.prompt: Match the old histories: true cousin of English brother; Indo-Aryan share-root replacement rather than cousin of sister; old eye word that also reaches English eye.
acceptedResponses: bharā — brother cousin; bhaiṇ — indo-aryan share-root replacement; akkh — old eye word and cousin of eye
bhara - brother; bhain - share-root replacement; akkh - eye cousin

feedback.correct: All three remembered family histories stayed separate.
feedback.incorrect: Repair one link at a time: brother-bharā, share-bhaiṇ, eye-akkh.

segments.text: Say the three meanings once more, then stop. No new item follows.
